visual_readings.visual_observation: Two antenna sketches: left nearly continuous curved segmented form labelled orthoceri; right sharply elbowed form labelled gonitoceri with a terminal club. The original printed leaders label club, scape and funiculus; preserve their placement as drawn, even where interpretation against the body definitions would be uncertain. Diagram shows contrasting arrangement, not a scale measurement or proof of taxonomic affinity.

Viewed preserved image: two drawn flowering stalks, the left long and straight, the right with conspicuously curved basal end. No printed labels or scale. Illustrates the straight versus curved-at-base diagnostic character discussed for Drosera; do not assign species labels solely from the unlabelled drawing.

Viewed cross-section with raised shell, a labelled ligament, three a marks, shaded underlying support and a central depression. It accompanies P1 distinction between marginal erosion and central hollow. No scale or newly inferred chemical mechanism is supplied by the drawing.

Viewed schematic female outline with Mouth and orifice into sack labels and a Males label pointing toward a cross at one side; another cross lies on the other side. It illustrates P10 male attachment positions, not the anatomy of the reduced male itself.

Viewed unlabelled sketch of an inclined small body above a horizontal surface, with a dotted outline below the surface. Read with P11 proposed initial position and burrow; angle, scale and depth are not quantitatively specified.

Root viewed the actual black-line sketch. A broad upper outline narrows to a pointed lower end with several parallel strokes; an inner notched tubular shape bears the label (a) below a small opening near the top. It accompanies Darwin apparent internal organ in the probosciform larval mouth, not a proven transverse articulation or an independently observed Bate illustration.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Three black line outlines labelled (a), (B), (C): first narrow simple taper, second wider upright form with short side projections, third central blade with two prominent lateral stipules. Matches successive Lathyrus seedling scale-leaves in body; not cotyledon drawings, no dimensions or scale.

Two schematic panels: A/B/C terrain with F volcano, B–D and G relative sea levels and deep K–L baseline; lower H mound, p/q marine surfaces, curved m/n/o beneath m-prime/o-prime. No measured scale; illustrates regional subsidence and local volcanic uplift.
H is a low central swell with q at left and p at right, stippled marine beds at the flanks above baselines; this is the hypothetical littoral-deposit comparison, not quantitative data.
Grand Canary labelled section: inclined marine beds overlap older subaerial rocks, rising terrain to the right; no numerical dimensions. Supports relative stratigraphic geometry only.

Truncated body at left has a row of short vertebral marks continuing into a narrow upward/projecting upper tail lobe; rounded larger lobe below. No scale or labels. Illustrates Dana report of juvenile gar-pike tail and proposed later loss of upper extension, not direct proof of a universal developmental law.
